name: Red Linen Bandana
summary: Across Elwynn Forest, the red linen bandana marks the Defias Brotherhood and hides its wearers' faces. Sara Timberlain at the Eastvale Logging Camp wants the cloth for garments and bandages.

sections.title: Mark of the Defias
sections.body: In Northshire Valley, initiates and common thugs wear coarse burlap masks. The crimson linen marks the allegiance of full operatives to Edwin VanCleef's rogue fraternity. It also signals rebellion against Stormwind's crown.

sections.title: Repurposed Cloth
sections.body: Sara Timberlain asks travelers to gather bandanas from outlaw encampments. The masks are tied to bandits, but their linen is respectable. Washed and worked with a needle, the cloth can become sturdy clothing and bandages for the forest's working folk.

faq.q: Why do the Defias wear red linen bandanas?
faq.answer: Defias operatives wear red linen bandanas to hide their faces. The cloth also marks their allegiance to Edwin VanCleef's brotherhood and their defiance of Stormwind.

faq.q: How do these differ from the masks worn in Northshire?
faq.answer: Northshire Valley thugs wear coarse burlap masks. Established Defias operatives across Elwynn Forest wear finer red linen.

faq.q: Who wants to collect these bandanas?
faq.answer: Sara Timberlain at the Eastvale Logging Camp wants the bandanas. She washes and unravels the masks to weave practical garments.

faq.q: Which enemies carry red linen bandanas?
faq.answer: Defias operatives across Elwynn Forest carry red linen bandanas. They include Defias Bandits, Ambushers, Rogue Wizards, dockworkers, and ringleaders such as Morgan the Collector.

angles.text: In rural Elwynn, weavers can turn the linen from bandit masks into working clothes.
As a rogue, you know the crimson cloth tied across the lower face. It marks highwaymen and cutpurses in the woods around the capital.
